items.requirement: State the research question: How does token-level highlighting of AI-generated code affect how users review and edit suggestions, and does highlighting likely edits work better than highlighting low-probability tokens?
items.quote:
we explore the value of token-level highlighting in a code generation
scenario.

items.requirement: Explain that the edit model predicts which tokens users are likely to edit, using preliminary data from nine coders who corrected Codex outputs until the tasks were completed properly.
items.quote:
Coders were asked to edit the Codex output until the task was completed
properly.

items.requirement: Describe the study sample and tasks: 30 employees of a large US technology company with Python experience completed three easy LeetCode tasks, with task order and tool-to-task assignments randomized.
items.quote:
Participants
were asked to complete three coding tasks, selected from Leetcode’s “easy” setting [10]

items.requirement: Identify the three presentation conditions using the same Davinci-002 Codex model: Prediction only with no highlighting, Generation probability highlighting at a 71% threshold, and Edit model highlighting at a 66% threshold. State that the thresholds matched total highlight counts across the three tasks for the two highlighting conditions.
items.quote:
We chose the highlighting thresholds such that the total number of highlights shown across
all three tasks for each condition were equivalent.

items.requirement: Report mean task times of 8.59 minutes for Edit model, 9.27 for Prediction only, and 9.61 for Generation probability under the 10-minute cap. Distinguish the significant Edit model advantage over Generation probability (p = 0.003) from the trend versus Prediction only (p = 0.06).
items.quote:
The difference between the two highlighting conditions is highly significant
(p = 0.003)

items.requirement: Use token survival, meaning a token remained untouched, to show more localized editing. Survival for non-highlighted tokens was 0.87 for Edit model, 0.81 for Generation probability, and 0.79 for Prediction only. Survival for highlighted tokens was 0.35 for Edit model and 0.74 for Generation probability.
items.quote:
Survival of tokens in each condition, separated
by whether the token was highlighted or not.

items.requirement: Report that participants rated Edit model highlights more favorably than Generation probability highlights (3.94 versus 2.88, p = 0.001) on 7-point items about helpfulness, willingness to pay, and distraction, with distraction reverse-coded.
items.quote:
Here we find an average response of 3.94 for
the edit conditions vs 2.88 for generation probability condition (Fig 1c)

items.requirement: State that the edit model was trained on the same AI-generated completions evaluated in the study and that comparable effects for a general-purpose model on unseen tasks remain unverified.
items.quote:
our work relies
on a closed-world edit model, learned on the very AI-generations evaluated in our study.

items.requirement: State that whether faster completion, more targeted edits, and higher preference translate into more accurate human oversight or reduced automation bias remains untested.
items.quote:
it remains to be demonstrated that the observed benefits (task completion time,
targeted edits, preference), translate to important high-level outcomes such as more accurate human
oversight and reduced automation bias.
